AppearancePatch.description: `[appearance]` in a [`SettingsPatch`]: its schema only, since `config::validate` reads the JSON itself.

theme.description: `appearance.theme`: light, dark, or the desktop's choice.

Comment.description: A comment in a task's thread (spec §9). The user's comments are delivered to the task's agent; an agent's are a record and never delivered.

author.description: Who wrote it: the user, or an agent from its pane.

author_agent.description: The agent that wrote it, when that is `claude` or `codex`.

author_pane.description: The pane it was written from; `None` for the user's, and once the pane is gone.

delivered_at.description: When it was delivered to an agent; always `None` for an agent's comment.

delivered_to_pane.description: The pane it was delivered to.

seen_at.description: When the user saw it; `None` while an agent's comment is new to the user. The user's own comments are seen when written.

DeleteWorkspaceError.description: `DELETE /v1/workspaces/{id}`'s error: dropshot's error body, plus the dirty report when `error_code` is `dirty` (409).

dirty.description: What deleting would lose; set only with `error_code` `dirty`.

DeviceSignIn.description: `POST /v1/github/device`: the code the user enters on GitHub to sign in.

uncommitted.description: Changed, staged and untracked files, as `git status --porcelain` prints them.

unpushed_branches.description: Local branches with commits that are on no remote, by name.

DirtyReport.description: The git repos under a workspace's dir that hold work not on any remote.

repos.description: Only the dirty repos; an empty list means deleting loses nothing git knows about.

GhLogin.description: Whether the daemon has a GitHub token GitHub accepts (spec §8).

oneOf.description: A token GitHub accepted, or one it couldn't be asked about yet.
No token from any source, or GitHub rejected the one found. The GUI shows a banner.

GithubAuthInfo.description: `GET /v1/github/auth`: where the GitHub token comes from, and whose it is. Never the token or the OAuth client ID.

client_id_set.description: Whether the keyring or `AGENTDECK_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID` gives an OAuth client ID, so Sign in with GitHub can start.

env_var.description: `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`, whichever is set (`GH_TOKEN` when both are), also while a saved token overrides it.

login.description: The token's GitHub user; absent while there's no token, GitHub rejected it, or it couldn't be asked.

rejected.description: Whether GitHub rejected the token `source` gives (revoked or expired). A token GitHub couldn't be asked about has no `login` either, but isn't rejected.

scopes.description: The token's scopes, from `X-OAuth-Scopes`; absent for a token that sends none (a fine-grained one).

source.description: The source the token comes from.

client_id.description: The client ID of the user's GitHub OAuth App, with Device Flow on.

token.description: A GitHub token: a classic one, or a fine-grained one.

GuiPatch.description: `[gui]` in a [`SettingsPatch`]: its schema only, since `config::validate` reads the JSON itself.

confirm_quit.description: `gui.confirm_quit`: whether closing the window or Quit asks first while an agent runs, since agents keep running after the GUI quits.

queued.description: True when it waits for the pane to be idle; false when it was typed.

oneOf.description: Once the pane is idle, done or blocked; at once if it already is.

Instruction.description: Standing context for every agent in a workspace (spec §9): it goes into every launch prompt there and stays until deleted.

Layout.description: A tab's split tree. Every pane appears once; [`Layout::split`] keeps it that way.

pane.description: The pane writing it: the comment is then that pane's agent's. Without it, the user's.

agent.description: Which agent: required for agent panes, absent for shells.

argv.description: The command. A shell pane without one runs `$SHELL`, else `/bin/sh`; an `other` agent pane needs one; `claude` and `codex` panes take none, since agentdeck builds theirs.

cwd.description: The absolute working directory, which must exist.

tab_id.description: The tab to add it to. The caller places it in the tab's layout.

task_id.description: A task to link. A `claude` or `codex` pane's launch prompt carries its title and body.

layout.description: The initial split tree, if any.

workspace_id.description: The workspace to link; the inbox when absent.

dir.description: An existing absolute directory to attach. Without it, agentdeck creates a scratch dir.

Pane.description: A terminal in a tab, running an agent CLI or a shell.

argv.description: The command as first launched, launch prompt included. A resumed pane runs its agent's resume command, or a fresh shell, instead.

cwd.description: The working directory it was launched in.

exit_code.description: The exit code, once the process has exited.

hosted_agent.description: The agent a shell pane hosts: `claude` or `codex` while the user's own is its foreground process, else null. Its kind stays `shell`; it runs that agent's state rules and takes the task's comments meanwhile (spec §3, §7).

session_id.description: The agent's session id: chosen at launch for `claude`, found after launch for `codex` (null until Codex has written its session file).

state.description: The agent state; a shell is `working` while it prints and `unknown` otherwise.

title.description: The title the program set, or empty.

submit.description: Submits `text` as a message: types it as one bracketed paste when the program turned bracketed paste on (else as is), then presses Enter in a write of its own, after a pause. Claude Code and Codex read text arriving with its Enter as a paste and keep the Enter as a newline. False when absent.

text.description: Typed into the terminal as is, unless `submit`.

PanePatch.description: `PATCH /v1/panes/{id}`: the task to link the pane to, or null to unlink it. `task_id` is required, so an empty body can't unlink a pane by accident.

task_id.description: A task in the pane's workspace that isn't done, or null.

PaneRun.description: What `POST /v1/panes/{id}/respawn` runs in an exited pane.

oneOf.description: The pane's agent again: claude and codex resume their session when it is known, else start fresh with a new launch prompt; an `other` agent runs its argv again. Agent panes only.
A shell, which turns the pane into a shell pane.

PrClose.description: `POST /v1/prs/close`: the PR tasks whose PRs to close on GitHub.

task_ids.description: The tasks, each a PR task whose PR is open; the results come back in this order.

error.description: Why it didn't: GitHub's message, why the request failed, "Not an open PR" or "Not signed in to GitHub". `None` when it closed.

PrCloseResults.description: `POST /v1/prs/close`'s answer: one result per task asked for, in the order asked.

PrSyncPatch.description: `[pr_sync]` in a [`SettingsPatch`]: its schema only, since `config::validate` reads the JSON itself.

PrSyncProgress.description: How far a running PR sync is through the viewer's PRs.

prs.description: PRs this sync expects, from the search's count; `0` until the first page answers.

prs_done.description: PRs read and stored so far.

stage.description: What the sync is doing now.

PrSyncSettings.description: `[pr_sync]`: which open PRs PR sync keeps (spec §8).

max_age_days.description: `pr_sync.max_age_days`: only open PRs GitHub updated in the last this many days sync; `0` for every open PR.

PrSyncStage.description: What a running PR sync is doing.

oneOf.description: Reading the list or the search, page by page; `prs_done` counts.
Fetching reviews and checks by number, after the last page.

PrSyncStatus.description: `GET /v1/prs/status` and `POST /v1/prs/sync`: the GitHub login and the last sync.

last_error.description: Why the most recent sync failed; `None` when it succeeded or none has run.

last_synced_at.description: When the last successful sync finished; `None` until one has.

login.description: Whether there's a token GitHub accepts.

max_age_days.description: How many days since GitHub last updated an open PR it may be and still sync: the setting `pr_sync.max_age_days` as it is now; `0` for no cutoff.

progress.description: How far the sync running now is; `None` while none runs.

PullRequest.description: The GitHub pull request behind a PR task, as PR sync last saw it (spec §8).

checks.description: The head commit's rolled-up checks; `None` when it has none.

head_ref.description: The branch the PR merges from.

number.description: The PR's number in that repo.

repo.description: `owner/name` of the repo the PR targets.

review.description: The review decision; `None` when the repo requires no review.

synced_at.description: When PR sync last saw the PR.

updated_at.description: When the PR last changed on GitHub.

Settings.description: `GET /v1/settings`, and what `PATCH /v1/settings` answers: every setting with the value the daemon uses (spec §2).

overridden_by_env.description: The dotted keys (`pr_sync.max_age_days`) whose value comes from an environment variable, not `config.toml`. A PATCH of one is written to the file, but the variable still wins until the daemon runs without it.

SettingsPatch.description:
`PATCH /v1/settings`: the settings to change, by section; the rest stay as they are.

The schema is typed, but each section is read as plain JSON so that a value or key the daemon doesn't take is a 400 `invalid_setting` naming its dotted key, not a parse error.

Tab.description: A tab in a workspace, holding a split tree of panes.

layout.description: The split tree; `None` until the tab has a pane.

position.description: Sort key among the workspace's tabs.

Task.description: An item in the one global task list.

done_at.description: When the task last moved to done; `None` while it isn't done.

pr.description: The pull request behind a PR task; `None` for a plain task.

unseen_agent_comments.description: Agents' comments on the task the user hasn't seen yet.

workspace_id.description: The linked workspace; `None` puts the task in the inbox.

title.description: A new title. A PR task's title is GitHub's: only its own title is accepted.

workspace_id.description: Where to move it: a workspace that isn't archived, or null for the inbox. Absent leaves it where it is.

TaskPlace.description: A workspace's id, or null for the inbox.

TerminalPatch.description: `[terminal]` in a [`SettingsPatch`]: its schema only, since `config::validate` reads the JSON itself.

file_opener.description: A new `terminal.file_opener`: a command holding `{path}` in an argument.

`terminal.file_opener`: the command a `secondary`-click on a file path in a pane runs, split into words as a shell would and never run through a shell. `{path}` is the file's absolute path, `{line}` and `{col}` where the path names them (else `1`).

oneOf.description: Follow the desktop's light or dark setting.

TokenEnvVar.description: An environment variable that gives the daemon a GitHub token.

TokenSource.description: Where the daemon's GitHub token comes from (spec §8), the first that gives one.

oneOf.description: A token saved in the system keyring: pasted, or from Sign in with GitHub.

UnpushedBranch.description: A local branch holding commits that are on no remote.

commits.description: How many of its commits are on no remote branch, whether or not it has an upstream.

Workspace.description: A free-form unit of work with its own directory.

archived_at.description: When the workspace was archived; archived workspaces keep their data.

dir.description: The absolute path of the workspace's directory.

dir_owned.description: True when agentdeck created `dir` as a scratch dir, so deleting the workspace removes it.

slug.description: Unique, derived from the name at creation; names a scratch dir.

name.description: A new display name. The slug and the dir stay as they are.
